label: Gemini CLI
description: One conversation with Gemini CLI, Google's coding agent: three conversations are three nodes. Wire `agent` and `stream` into an AskAgent and talk to it in a Loop; end the loop with a CloseBus on `stream`, which ends this node's part of the run. With no `computer`, Gemini CLI runs on your machine (a local install only) from your own install of `gemini` with your own login, working in `folder`. If `gemini` is missing, weft installs it into a folder of its own, shared by the whole machine, before the node runs. With a `computer` wired, it is installed and run inside that computer, which a cloud install needs, and it logs in with the connection on `access`. The folder is always trusted (`--skip-trust`): in a folder it was never told to trust, Gemini CLI starts none of your program's tools and refuses `accept_edits` and `bypass`. It has no question tool here, so it asks in plain text, in its reply. Its card shows what it is doing and a Start over button. What is exposed: the permission mode, the model, extra folders and a container to run its tools in; the rest of Gemini CLI's own settings stay in its `settings.json`. Your program's tools reach Gemini CLI's model as `mcp_weft_<tool>`, Gemini CLI's own naming for a tool it did not build, and come back to your program under their plain names; in the `plan` permission setting it gives its model no outside tools at all. Gemini CLI cannot let a program's tool take one of its own tools' places, so a tool named like one of them (`read_file`, `run_shell_command`, `google_web_search` and the rest of this node's list) is refused when the program is built.

inputs.name: computer
inputs.description: A Computer to run Gemini CLI in. Left out, it runs on your machine, which only a local install has. Several agents may share one computer.

inputs.name: access
inputs.description: A GeminiCliAccess's `access`: a Gemini API key or a Vertex AI key. Required with a `computer`. Left out on your machine, Gemini CLI uses the login already on it, your Google account included.

inputs.name: folder
inputs.label: Folder
inputs.description: The folder Gemini CLI works in. On your machine it is required, and must exist. In a computer it is a path inside the computer, its home folder when left out.

inputs.name: program
inputs.label: Program
inputs.description: On your machine: the Gemini CLI program to run, when it is not the `gemini` on your PATH or the one weft installs (an install of your own, a version you keep for this). A path on your machine, so it cannot go with a `computer`.

inputs.name: permission
inputs.label: Permissions
inputs.description: What Gemini CLI may do without asking. `ask`: every edit and command it would put to a person comes out of AskAgent as a question. `accept_edits`: file edits go ahead, the rest asks. `plan`: it only reads and plans, and changes nothing. `bypass`: nothing asks, nothing is refused; for a computer, which is the wall around it.

inputs.name: model
inputs.label: Model
inputs.description: The Gemini model to use, by name. Left out, Gemini CLI's own default.

inputs.name: streamBy
inputs.label: Stream by
inputs.description: What goes out on `stream`: `message`, one event per whole message, tool use and result, so a run waiting on a long step sleeps; `token`, every piece of text as it is written too, which keeps the run awake while the agent writes.

inputs.name: addDirs
inputs.label: Extra folders
inputs.description: Folders besides `folder` Gemini CLI may read and change.

inputs.name: sandbox
inputs.label: Sandbox
inputs.description: Run its tools in a container of this kind, which needs that runtime on the machine it runs on. Left out, they run without one.

outputs.name: agent
outputs.description: The agent's handle: wire it into AskAgent's `agent`. Baked: made when the infra is started.

outputs.name: stream
outputs.description: Everything the agent does in this run, as AskAgent sends it. Wire it into every AskAgent of the loop, and into a CloseBus after the loop: the run's part of this node ends when it does.

then.message: GeminiCli '{id}' runs on the machine weft runs on, which a cloud install does not have; wire a Computer into `computer`.
GeminiCli '{id}' runs in a computer, where no login is waiting for it; give it a GeminiCliAccess on `access`.
GeminiCli '{id}' works on your machine, so it needs a `folder` to work in.
GeminiCli '{id}' has a `permission` it does not know; pick one of ask, accept_edits, plan, bypass.
GeminiCli '{id}' has a `streamBy` it does not know; pick message or token.
GeminiCli '{id}' runs in a computer, where `program`, a path on your machine, means nothing; leave `program` out, the computer installs Gemini CLI itself.
